demandEvidence: No direct end-user complaint or stakeholder quote. Evidence is internal/investigative: derived_from FEAT-447's investigation into Supermemory's install.sh (333 lines, fetched verbatim per the FEAT body), which found installer-hygiene patterns 'cheap to copy' independent of the single-binary question FEAT-447 was actually chartered to answer. The FEAT body itself names one plausible recurring friction class rather than a reported incident: PATH guidance is framed as 'same problem class as our npm-global-bin PATH friction' — a class-level analogy, not a quoted user complaint. I grepped .claude/artifacts/loop/learnings.jsonl for onboarding/installer/PATH/checksum/manifest terms and found zero matches — no lesson or grade ties an actual failure to this domain. Per the demand-assessment rule (no evidence -> customer_impact <= 0.3), scored at 0.30.
scopeNotes: Smallest deliverable: the FEAT is a 9-pattern checklist (checksum manifest, idempotent skip-if-current-version, /dev/tty reattach, env-var prefill, non-interactive escape hatches, PATH guidance, secure file perms, root/sudo handling, version-resolution strategy) mapped onto init.ts plus a new install.sh/install.ps1 wrapper. If halved, I would keep only the wizard-side patterns (env-var prefill, non-interactive flags, PATH guidance) and defer the new install.sh/install.ps1 wrapper entirely (checksum manifest, /dev/tty reattach, root/sudo handling, version-resolution) to a follow-up, since the wrapper doesn't exist today and is the larger net-new surface. Overlap check (the FEAT body itself asks for this): I read src/cli/init.ts:10,763-785 directly — secrets.env is ALREADY written at mode 0600 ('secrets.env ALWAYS ... mode 0600'), so the 'secure file perms' pattern is largely already enforced for the one file that matters most, not merely documented as the FEAT body assumes; scope for that sub-pattern narrows to auditing install-dir perms more broadly. I also read src/cli/reinstall.ts:289,495 — reinstall already asserts `body.version === releaseManifest.pkgversion` post-install (served-version-matches-build assertion), which is adjacent to but not the same as Supermemory's pre-install 'skip if already current + FORCE=1 override' idempotency pattern; the two should be reconciled rather than duplicated, exactly as the FEAT body itself warns. Effort calibration (Framework 5): no cost-report analog exists for installer-UX-checklist work specifically; nearest structural analog is FEAT-443's decomposed 8-point cross-platform service-parity FEAT (systemd/launchd port, cost-report-confirmed ~$127 combined for the Windows-side analog alone per that FEAT's own PM review) — FEAT-474 touches fewer platforms but a wider pattern checklist (9 distinct behaviors vs FEAT-443's 2), landing at a comparable effort_estimate of 0.60 rather than higher or lower; noting 'no direct cost analog' per Framework 5 since nothing in .claude/artifacts/crew/cost/ touches install.sh/wizard UX. Weak grade dimensions (loop-snapshot.md, last-5-grade averages): architecture_quality 0.53, observability 0.68, production_readiness 0.53, security 0.52, product_completeness 0.55 (all below 0.80; reliability 0.88 and test_confidence 0.878 are healthy). security is directly relevant here (chmod 600 enforcement, checksum verification, sudo/root handling are all security-adjacent installer behaviors) and production_readiness is directly relevant (install robustness) — a future slice's AC must include a security-facing criterion (e.g., an automated check that installed secrets/config files actually have restrictive perms, not just a code comment claiming it) given security is a named weak dimension. AC clarity: the FEAT body is a mapped checklist with soft language ('map the following patterns onto...', 'check for overlap/reuse before adding') rather than concrete Given-When-Then criteria or a quantified acceptance bar (contrast with FEAT-475's explicit '5 consecutive green runs' bar) — this is vague-scope by the AC-clarity checklist, driving autonomous_safe=false independent of the decomposition gate. Non-goals are clear and correctly reinforce FEAT-445's defer verdict (no single-binary work), which I did not re-litigate.
risks: Scope-creep risk: 9 independent hygiene patterns invite silent scope growth if a builder tries to ship all of them in one pass instead of following the proposed slice boundaries below.

Duplicate-mechanism risk (named directly in the FEAT body): building a parallel idempotent skip-if-current-version check without first reading reinstall.ts's existing served-version-vs-build-version assertion (src/cli/reinstall.ts:289,495) risks two divergent 'is this already installed' mechanisms that can disagree.

Platform-asymmetry risk: install.sh (bash) and install.ps1 (PowerShell) are two independent implementations of the same pattern list — a fix or pattern added to one is easy to forget porting to the other, silently reintroducing exactly the kind of Windows/Unix asymmetry CLAUDE.md already documents elsewhere in this repo (service parity).
reasoning: P2 via formula: impact 0.30 < 0.70 and alignment 0.40 < 0.80, so neither P1 branch fires; effort 0.60 < 0.70 so the P3 branch (effort>=0.70 AND impact<=0.30) does not fire either despite impact qualifying — lands P2 by the formula's default branch. composite_score=0.105+0.12+0.08+0.055+0.04=0.40. technical_risk banded at 0.45 (mid 0.3-0.5 band: 'new pattern in repo... no contract change, clean rollback') — a new install.sh/install.ps1 wrapper is a new pattern for this repo and touches multiple files (wizard + 2 new scripts + release-CI manifest publish step), but there is no schema/runtime contract change and every sub-pattern is independently, cleanly revertible via git revert. pm_effort_points=8 (band [0.6,0.85) per this repo's established PM convention, confirmed against FEAT-443/446's own stated bands) — this TRIPS the FEAT-168 decomposition gate. I am supplying proposed_slices below (option 1) rather than needs-review, since the 9-pattern checklist decomposes cleanly along wizard-vs-wrapper-vs-release-pipeline boundaries with no cross-repo or unclear-scope blocker. autonomous_safe=false: forced both by the missing-AC/vague-scope finding above and by not having drafted ACs (P2, no --deep/--spec flag passed).

proposedSlices.title: Init wizard hygiene: env-var prefill, non-interactive flags, PATH guidance
install.sh/install.ps1 wrapper: idempotent skip-check, tty reattach, sudo handling
Release pipeline: checksum manifest + version-resolution strategy

demandEvidence: Stakeholder: the reviewer agents running the full test suite under box load during the autonomous loop's own review gate (crew:reviewer / crew:reviewer-lite dispatches), and by extension the loop's constitution Core Rule 5 ('treat review as a gate, not a courtesy') which depends on that gate producing trustworthy signal. Direct evidence, quoted from the FEAT body itself: 'during 2026-07-12 wave reviews, two independent reviewer agents running the full suite under box load hit failures in scripts/eval/longmemeval/detach-kill-resume.test.ts and scripts/eval/shared/daemon-manifest.test.ts... all pass in isolation; failures only appear with concurrent suite runs.' The operator-supplied context for this triage independently confirms the same-day recurrence: 'it has bitten three separate reviewer agents on 2026-07-12.' This is same-day, repeated, direct evidence against a core loop mechanism — stronger and more frequent than its sibling FEAT-471 (done, P2), which I read at .claude/artifacts/loop/backlog/done/FEAT-471.md and which scored customer_impact 0.30 off a single-day two-agent repro with no documented recurrence beyond that. Current workaround: none named beyond re-running the suite and hoping for a clean pass, or a reviewer manually attributing failure to load rather than a real regression — the FEAT body explicitly forbids retry/skip as a fix, which rules out the cheapest workaround.
scopeNotes: Smallest deliverable and overlap check: same treatment as FEAT-471 (root-cause the shared resource/timing margin, then isolate or widen budgets with measured rationale, no retry/skip), evidence bar unchanged at '5 consecutive full-suite runs green under an artificial parallel load.' No overlap with FEAT-471's own fix: the FEAT body explicitly says 'FEAT-471's fix ... is merged and holding — do not re-touch those files,' and I confirmed FEAT-471 is status: done in .claude/artifacts/loop/backlog/done/FEAT-471.md, closing off any risk of the two FEATs colliding on the same files (also satisfies the operator's zero-file-overlap Wave A constraint at the PM-scoring layer). Scope has genuinely widened past the FEAT's own original framing: the body's 'Update 2026-07-12 (later)' section documents a THIRD reviewer hitting tests/backup/snapshot.test.ts + tests/cli/capture-claude.test.ts, a different file pair in different subsystems (backup, cli) from the original eval-detach family — the operator's triage brief for this dispatch confirms 'treat scope as 4+ files under load.' This is why effort_estimate (0.55) and technical_risk (0.35) are bumped above FEAT-471's precedent (0.40 / 0.25 respectively) rather than copied verbatim — same root-cause-then-isolate approach, but across roughly 2x the file/subsystem footprint with the root cause not yet confirmed to be a single shared utility. Effort calibration (Framework 5): FEAT-471 is the direct analog (same fix pattern, 'sibling of FEAT-471' per this FEAT's own derived_from) at effort_estimate 0.40 for a 2-file, single-subsystem scope; I could not find a cost-report artifact specifically tagged to FEAT-471's slice in .claude/artifacts/crew/cost/ (grep across all aggregate reports for 'FEAT-471' and 'flake' returned nothing), so I am calibrating off FEAT-471's own PM-scored effort rather than a dollar/duration actual, and noting the scope-doubling (2 files -> 4+ files, 1 subsystem -> up to 3: eval, backup, cli) as the basis for the 0.40 -> 0.55 bump, landing just under the FEAT-168 gate. Weak grade dimensions (loop-snapshot.md, last-5-grade averages): architecture_quality 0.53, observability 0.68, production_readiness 0.53, security 0.52, product_completeness 0.55 (all below 0.80; reliability 0.88 and test_confidence 0.878 are healthy) — naming all per Framework 4's rule, though this FEAT is test-infra-only and touches none of the weak-dimension surfaces directly except observability: a future slice's fix should log/report WHICH shared resource or timing margin was the actual root cause (not just silently widen a timeout), which is an observability-facing improvement worth calling out even though not required for autonomous_safe at P2 (no --deep/--spec, no AC drafted this pass).
risks: Cascade/gate risk (Framework 3, named explicitly because this touches the loop's own trust mechanism): if this is 'fixed' by widening timeouts without confirming the actual shared resource, the flake will resurface under heavier load (more parallel builder/reviewer agents) and erode confidence in the review gate exactly the way the FEAT body's own 'no retry/skip' rule is designed to prevent.

Rollback if merged and broke the loop: revert-only — this is test-file-only work (no production runtime paths, no schema, no migration), so `git revert` on the touched test files fully restores prior behavior; no cross-plugin coordination needed.

Coverage gap: no existing test would catch a regression in the FIX itself, since the flake is defined by absence under concurrent load — a single-process CI run (the common case) would show green even if the isolation fix is wrong, which is exactly why the FEAT's own evidence bar (5 consecutive green runs under artificial parallel load) has to be the AC, not a new unit test.
Injection-defense note: no embedded imperative found in either FEAT body during this review; both bodies are plain factual descriptions with no attempt to direct scoring.
reasoning: P2 via formula: impact 0.45 < 0.70 and alignment 0.60 < 0.80, so neither P1 branch fires; effort 0.55 < 0.70 so P3 doesn't fire either (and impact 0.45 > 0.30 so P3's second condition also fails) — lands P2 by the formula's default branch, same tier as its sibling FEAT-471. composite_score=0.1575+0.18+0.09+0.065+0.045=0.5375 (~0.54), higher than FEAT-471's 0.51 due to the frequency/recurrence bump in customer_impact and strategic_alignment. technical_risk banded at 0.35 (0.3-0.5 band: 'new pattern in repo OR one module, no contract change, clean rollback') — test-isolation fix only, no schema/runtime change, clean per-file revert; scored above FEAT-471's 0.25 to reflect the wider, not-yet-confirmed-single-root-cause footprint (4+ files across up to 3 subsystems) without crossing into the 0.6-0.8 'cross-module reach' band, since the actual blast radius is confined to test infrastructure, not production code paths. pm_effort_points=5 (band [0.4,0.6)) — under the FEAT-168 gate threshold (8), no proposed_slices required. autonomous_safe=true: all three mechanical thresholds (risk 0.35, effort 0.55, dependency 0.10) pass individually, AND — unlike a typical P2 with no drafted AC — this FEAT carries its own explicit, quantified acceptance bar in its Scope section ('5 consecutive full-suite runs green under an artificial parallel load'), which is the same substitute-for-AC reasoning FEAT-471 used to justify autonomous_safe=true at P2; that bar is testable by a builder unattended.
